title: Bad credentials retry the hub login forever: no ConfigEntryAuthFailed, no reauth flow
why_top: It leads every metric that counts here — 52.5 adjusted against 23.4 for the runner-up, 17.5 per round against 7.8, and it is the only idea three different agents chose to champion across three rounds. It is also the only idea whose debate actually converged on a buildable answer: C3 asked whether pytapo even exposes a distinguishable rejected-login signature, Priya's devil's-advocate turn showed the obvious string marker is not one (the same "Invalid authentication data" literal appears on the -40413 device_confirm path after MAX_LOGIN_RETRIES), and Ada replaced it with a type-level rule that fails safe toward retry. I confirmed the underlying defect firsthand: `grep -rn "async_step_reauth\|ConfigEntryAuthFailed" custom_components/ tests/` returns nothing, and `__init__.py:196-202` funnels every `connect()` failure into `ConfigEntryNotReady` with the message "Cannot reach the H500" — so a changed camera-account password produces a permanent backoff loop of fresh logins against hardware this repo documents as wedging under exactly that.
value_rationale: Nearest the 55-anchor — an evidenced, well-scoped conformance fix. Up from it: the defect is verified in every particular and the harm is user-visible and self-inflicted on fragile hardware (repeated logins are the documented wedge trigger), and Home Assistant's reauth flow is the standard, reversible mechanism. Down from it: five files (api.py, __init__.py, config_flow.py, strings.json, translations/en.json), no failing test pins it today, and the classifier is a heuristic judgement call that must be built to fail safe. Net → 58.
decomposition: In api.py's connect(), raise a dedicated H500AuthError only on the type-level rule Ada landed in round 3 — a pytapo error carrying an error_code that survives its own retries. Everything else (OSError, RequestException, socket timeout, and the bare ValueError a garbage response produces) stays untyped so the caller keeps retrying; the wedge shape must never reach the auth branch.
In __init__.py:196-202, catch H500AuthError and raise ConfigEntryAuthFailed; leave every other exception on the existing ConfigEntryNotReady path with its current message and client.close() cleanup.
Add async_step_reauth / async_step_reauth_confirm to config_flow.py, reusing the connect()+cameras() validation already in async_step_user, then update the entry data and reload.
Add the reauth step and error keys to BOTH strings.json and translations/en.json — the two files are already 102 keys out of sync, so writing only one continues the rot.

Extend tests/test_config_flow.py with three cases: a wedge-shaped failure stays ConfigEntryNotReady, an error_code-bearing rejection raises ConfigEntryAuthFailed, and the reauth flow rewrites the stored password.
premise_notes: Verified "overstated", not false: the defect holds in every load-bearing particular (I re-confirmed the bare-Exception handler and the total absence of reauth machinery), but round 3's string-marker argument was wrong — "Invalid authentication data" is neither auth-specific nor uniform — costing a −1.5 partial dock; the type-level classifier and the -40413 attack both survive.
metrics_note: Trusted raw. All three contending ideas were active in all three rounds (rounds_active 3/3, well above the 60% bar), so no idea is materially less-tested and raw is the honest measure; it and per_round agree on the winner anyway (56 and 17.5 versus 23.4 and 7.8). Champion counts do differ (3 versus 1), so per_arg deserves a word: frontend-cards-2 scores 7.8 per argument against ha-conformance-1's 5.8. I did not let that decide it — per_arg penalizes an idea precisely for attracting more advocates, and the extra arguments here were not padding: two of them (the -40413 attack and the type-level answer to C3) are what moved the idea from unproven to buildable. The gap is too wide for the metric choice to matter regardless, so no tie-break was needed.
strongest_dissent: C5, round 3: "The probe-based variant recreates the very regression it claims to close: api.py returns 'wedged' or 'silent' whenever the hub accepts the TCP connection but fails the exchange, so 'probe is not unreachable therefore the hub refused our credentials' classifies a wedged H500 — the documented failure mode — as an auth failure and stops retrying. Any shipped classifier must treat wedged/silent as not-authenticated-failure, and nobody has stated that." This stands, and I confirmed the code it rests on: api.py:107-123 returns "silent" on timeout and "wedged" on ConnectionError or an empty read, and check_media_port targets 8800 — a different service from the one connect() logs into. The build must take the type-level route and drop the probe variant entirely.

minority.why_lost: Lost on a 29-point adjusted gap (23.4 against 52.5) with one champion to three. Its premise came back clean — I have no quarrel with the defect — but it never grew past round 1: the judge flagged round 3 as holding the same ground already held in rounds 1 and 2 (D5), and across all three rounds the impact case was asserted rather than shown. Nobody demonstrated a user actually watching a clip through a 60-second boundary; the mechanism is proven, the frequency is not.
minority.flip_condition: If the auth classifier cannot be made to fail safe — that is, if no type-level signal reliably separates rejected credentials from a wedged hub, leaving every candidate rule able to strand a briefly-offline hub in a stopped entry — then ha-conformance-1's value inverts into a regression risk on the exact hardware this repo documents as fragile, and frontend-cards-2 wins: a single guard in the H500Base _player path covering six cards, with tests/test_cards.mjs:288-294 already driving _playing as a harness, and nothing to misclassify.
